label: Ignatius of Antioch addresses the church at Smyrna

date.note: Ignatius wrote en route to martyrdom at Rome. Eusebius (Hist. eccl. 3.36) places the journey under Trajan (reigned 98–117), traditionally c. 107–110; the range brackets the later part of Trajan's reign. A minority redates the letters to c. 125–150 (Barnes 2008).

secondary.cite: Harnack, Mission and Expansion, vol. 2, pp. 185–186

notes: The letter to the Smyrnaeans. Ignatius was hosted by the Smyrna church during his journey and wrote several letters from there. Independent of the Apocalypse's letter to Smyrna (lit-apocalypse-smyrna) and ~15 years later. His letter to Polycarp (lit-ignatius-polycarp) attests the same church a second time, addressed to its bishop.
